descriptionChirho: To break or violate a covenant, agreement, or commandment, rendering it no longer in force by transgression (Hifil active, Arabic نقض, Swahili vunja).
To annul, nullify, or invalidate a vow, decree, or obligation by authoritative declaration, making it legally void (Hifil active, Arabic أبطل, Swahili batilisha).
To frustrate, thwart, or bring to nothing the counsel, plans, or purposes of another, causing them to fail (Hifil active, Spanish frustrar, Arabic إفشال/إبطال).
To be broken, to fail, or to come to nothing, used of plans, covenants, or purposes that are rendered ineffective (Hofal passive and intransitive Hifil).
To shatter or break someone to pieces with intensive, physical force, expressing violent destruction of a person (Piel intensive, Arabic فتّت, Swahili katakata).
